security_audit.summary: The static external-command and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, examples, and normal validation control flow. The review did find real packaging and path-handling risks in the helper scripts that could expose files or write outside the intended output path.

remediation.issue: init_skill.py accepts skill names without enforcing the documented naming rules.
remediation.suggestion: Validate skill_name against the hyphen-case pattern before constructing paths, and reject absolute paths or traversal segments.

remediation.issue: package_skill.py recursively packages all files under the selected folder.
remediation.suggestion: Add default exclusions for hidden files, secrets, caches, and build output. Refuse symlinks that resolve outside the skill directory.

remediation.issue: quick_validate.py performs only minimal structural checks.
remediation.suggestion: Extend validation to detect unresolved TODO placeholders, oversized resources, unsafe symlinks, and sensitive filenames before packaging.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Allows Path Traversal
semantic_findings.description: init_skill.py appends the user-supplied skill name to the output path without enforcing the documented hyphen-case rules. A name containing traversal segments or an absolute path could write generated files outside the intended directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script documents strict name requirements but passes sys.argv[1] directly into path construction. The resulting directory is then created and populated with files.

semantic_findings.title: Recursive Packaging Can Include Unintended Files
semantic_findings.description: package_skill.py recursively adds every file under the selected skill directory to the zip archive. Without exclusions or symlink checks, hidden files, local secrets, or linked files outside the skill can be included accidentally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rglob loop writes each file it sees into the package with no ignore list, secret scan, or symlink guard. This is a common release-packaging data exposure risk.

content.user_title: Create AI Skills with Structured Guidance
content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills is hard when structure, examples, and packaging steps are unclear. This skill guides planning, scaffolding, editing, validation, and packaging for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains the anatomy of a skill, including SKILL.md, scripts, references, and assets.
Guides users through concrete examples before choosing reusable skill resources.
Provides init_skill.py to scaffold a SKILL.md file and example resource directories.
Provides quick_validate.py for basic frontmatter and naming checks.
Provides package_skill.py to validate a skill and create a distributable zip file.
Recommends editing practices for concise, reusable AI instructions.
limitations: Generated templates still require project-specific content from the author.
The validator checks basic frontmatter and names only. It is not a full security audit.
Packaging includes files under the selected skill folder. Authors must remove secrets first.
The guidance is optimized for Claude-style skills and may need adaptation for other runtimes.

use_cases.title: Create a New Team Skill
use_cases.description: Plan a reusable workflow, scaffold the skill folder, and prepare it for review.

use_cases.title: Package a Skill for Sharing
use_cases.description: Validate required metadata and create a zip file for distribution.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review usage examples, move detailed material into resources, and refine SKILL.md instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a new skill for [task]. Ask the few key questions needed, then suggest the SKILL.md structure.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Skill Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these example user requests for my skill: [examples]. Recommend which scripts, references, and assets should be included.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold and Edit a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill named [skill-name] in [path], then help replace the template content with focused instructions and resources.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Package a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing skill at [path], identify structural issues, suggest fixes, validate it, and prepare it for packaging.

output_examples.input: Plan a skill that helps analysts summarize customer interviews.
output_examples.output: A proposed skill structure with workflow sections, reference files for interview rubrics, and asset suggestions for report templates.

output_examples.input: Prepare my skill folder for sharing with another team.
output_examples.output: A validation summary, a list of required metadata fixes, and packaging steps for a distributable archive.

output_examples.input: Improve this SKILL.md so another AI agent can use it reliably.
output_examples.output: A tighter instruction outline, clearer trigger guidance, and recommendations for moving long examples into reference files.

best_practices: Start from real user requests before deciding the skill structure.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move detailed material into references when appropriate.
Validate and review all packaged files before sharing the skill.
anti_patterns: Do not include every possible detail in SKILL.md when references would work better.
Do not leave generated TODO placeholders in a published skill.
Do not package secrets, private data, or unnecessary example files.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create reusable AI skills with clear instructions, resource folders, validation, and packaging steps.

faq.question: Does it generate a starter skill folder?
faq.answer: Yes. The included init script creates a SKILL.md template and example scripts, references, and assets folders.

faq.question: Can it validate a finished skill?
faq.answer: It includes a basic validator for frontmatter, required fields, and naming rules. Manual review is still required.

faq.question: Can it package a skill for distribution?
faq.answer: Yes. The package script validates the skill, then creates a zip archive from the selected skill folder.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: The guidance targets Claude-style skills and is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I check before sharing a package?
faq.answer: Review all included files, remove secrets and unused examples, and confirm the instructions match real user needs.
